key_insight: The paper introduces a direct quantum-circuit method to prepare the ν=1/3 Laughlin fractional quantum Hall state on arbitrary geometries, including the sphere, with lower gate cost than variational approaches.
engineering_relevance: It provides a more hardware-friendly route for realizing topological many-body states on near-term and fault-tolerant quantum devices, with pulse designs tailored to superconducting and Rydberg platforms.
method: Construct a direct circuit for exact preparation of the Laughlin state on the sphere geometry.
Use optimal control to generate experimentally feasible pulse sequences for superconducting and Rydberg hardware.
Compare resource usage against variational circuits, targeting fewer two-qubit gates and shallower depth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the proposed method significantly reduces two-qubit gate count and circuit depth relative to variational quantum circuit approaches and identifies feasible control protocols on two hardware platforms.
watch_item: Experimental performance may still depend on control fidelity and hardware-specific noise, so exact state preparation could be sensitive to implementation errors.
paper_title: Preparation of Fractional Quantum Hall States on Quantum Computers
